The authors compare several data augmentation approaches for the minority class, selecting the one that best improves recall in downstream logistic regression and other classifiers. CTGAN is run alongside SMOTE and a Gaussian Copula method as one of several class-imbalance augmentation baselines evaluated against the authors' own proposed technique.
paper-predicting-suicidal-ideation-plann.needs: Full text does not detail CTGAN's specific results/parameters, only names it as one of the compared augmentation techniques; unclear whether SDV's own GaussianCopula implementation (vs. the cited Song 2000 statistical paper) was actually used.

paper-prediction-cardiovascular-disease-.summary: This conference paper builds a TabNet-based deep learning model to predict cardiovascular disease risk in diabetic patients using NHANES survey data, addressing class imbalance in the dataset with a GAN-based approach, and uses SHAP to identify key risk factors such as waist circumference, age, and BMI. The paper states it 'employs Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) methods to address the prominent issue of sample imbalance,' citing the CTGAN paper as reference [10], but the extracted full text gives no further detail on how CTGAN was implemented or applied. CTGAN is cited as the GAN methodology referenced for oversampling minority (high-risk) cases, without visible evidence it was run via the SDV library itself.

paper-sok-privacy-preserving-synthesis-2.summary: This is a Systematization of Knowledge paper that surveys privacy-preserving data synthesis (PPDS) methods, unifying statistical and deep-learning-based approaches under a common taxonomy, and benchmarking several DL-based image synthesis methods to identify DP-MERF as an all-purpose approach. The paper's discussion of tabular synthesis describes CTGAN's mode-specific normalization technique in prose as prior work, with the meta-review noting no experiments on tabular data were conducted. CTGAN's variational-Gaussian-mixture-based normalization for numerical inputs is cited and described as related work, not run or benchmarked.

paper-groundwater-par-2024.summary: Generates synthetic groundwater level series from USGS National Water Information System records to support aquifer management where monitoring wells are sparse. It names the SDV framework explicitly and uses the Probabilistic AutoRegressive synthesizer, which makes this one of the clearest uses of PAR outside the first-party sequential work.

paper-warts-disease-treatment-suggestion.summary: This conference paper proposes a machine-learning and deep-learning framework that combines numerical and image data to classify wart treatment (cryotherapy vs. immunotherapy) for HPV-induced warts, achieving up to 91.67% accuracy on raw data. Because the original numerical dataset had only 90 points, the authors additionally used CTGAN alongside SMOTE to synthetically expand the dataset and tested classifiers on the combined data, though accuracy dropped when synthetic data was added. CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN from the SDV family, is run as a data-augmentation tool to increase dataset size, one of two synthetic-data-generation techniques compared in the study.
paper-warts-disease-treatment-suggestion.needs: Evidence does not specify whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package/library or a custom implementation was used; assumed api_user given no reimplementation details and standard terminology.

paper-synthetic-generation-technique-enh.summary: This paper forecasts daily rental demand for electric kickboards on Jeju Island by augmenting a small real-world time-series dataset with synthetic data, then feeding the combined data into an ensemble of CatBoost, Random Forest, and XGBoost regressors. The synthetic time-series data are generated using an 'improved CTGAN' model, with a reported hyperparameter table (generator_dim, discriminator_dim, batch_size, generator_lr, discriminator_lr) matching the CTGAN constructor. CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN from the SDV family, is run as the core data-augmentation generator whose synthetic output the entire empirical forecasting improvement depends on.

paper-artificial-intelligence-framework-.summary: This study develops a machine-learning framework to predict whether a wildfire will sustain propagation and whether it will transition to crown fire in southern Australian semiarid shrublands, comparing classifiers such as SVM, Naive Bayes and neural networks. To address limited and imbalanced fire behaviour data, the authors augment their training set with synthetic data generated via a Generative Adversarial Network approach, which improved SVM classification accuracy by up to 20%. The paper cites the SDV and TGAN papers in connection with this GAN-based tabular data augmentation step, though the full text needed to confirm whether the sdv-dev package itself was run was not available.
paper-artificial-intelligence-framework-.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev/TGAN package was actually run (api_user) or reimplemented/only cited alongside a custom GAN augmentation method.

paper-ensemble-oversampling-method-imbal.summary: This paper proposes an ensemble oversampling approach for imbalanced classification that incorporates prior knowledge into a generative adversarial network to synthesize minority-class samples. The method is evaluated on imbalanced datasets, positioning itself among GAN-based oversampling techniques. The work cites the TGAN paper (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) among its GAN-related references, but the evidence available does not show whether TGAN was actually run or merely cited as related work.
paper-ensemble-oversampling-method-imbal.needs: Full text or abstract needed to determine whether TGAN was run as a baseline/generator or only cited in related work; metadata_only evidence is insufficient to resolve integration type or affiliations.

paper-ctcn-credit-card-fraud-2023.summary: This paper proposes CTCN, a credit card fraud detection pipeline that combines an oversampling stage based on CTGAN with a Neighborhood Cleaning Rule filter and a Temporal Convolutional Network classifier to address severe class imbalance in transaction data. The authors train CTGAN on the minority (fraud) class to generate synthetic samples that match the real data distribution, then clean overlapping majority-class samples before classification, comparing this oversampling approach against SMOTE, ADASYN, and other resampling methods on three public credit card datasets. CTGAN is the generative model at the core of the oversampling algorithm, run to produce the synthetic fraud transactions that the entire empirical evaluation rests on.
paper-ctcn-credit-card-fraud-2023.needs: The Preliminary Knowledge section describes CTGAN's generator/critic loss in detail, which could indicate a from-scratch reimplementation rather than use of the sdv-dev package; no explicit library name, import, or constructor parameters are given, so api_user vs. port remains somewhat ambiguous.

paper-conditional-feature-importance-mix.summary: This paper distinguishes marginal from conditional feature importance measures and proposes combining the conditional predictive impact (CPI) framework with sequential knockoff sampling to handle mixed continuous/categorical data, demonstrating type I error control and high power via simulations and a real-world example. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing, in a single sentence noting that deep generative models for mixed data are an active research area, without being used for knockoff generation.
paper-conditional-feature-importance-mix.needs: Full text not available; only the abstract and citing sentence were seen, so any deeper engagement with CTGAN beyond this passing mention cannot be verified.

paper-dealing-bias-classification-can-20.summary: This conference paper investigates whether synthetically generated data can improve representation and reduce bias in classification tasks, addressing fairness concerns tied to imbalanced or underrepresented groups in training data. The metadata available does not reveal the specific experimental pipeline or generator architecture used. It cites the original Synthetic Data Vault paper (Patki et al., 2016), suggesting SDV's synthetic data generation framework is referenced as related or underlying work for producing representative synthetic data.
paper-dealing-bias-classification-can-20.needs: No full text or abstract available; cannot confirm whether SDV's software/library was actually run to generate data or merely cited as background on synthetic data frameworks.

paper-acgan-modified-auxiliary-classifie.summary: This paper proposes MS-ACGAN, a modified auxiliary classifier GAN designed to augment small, imbalanced schizophrenia microarray gene expression datasets to improve downstream classification performance. It cites CTGAN as related work on GAN-based synthetic data generation for tabular/structured data. CTGAN is referenced only in passing as prior art, with no evidence of it being run or benchmarked.
paper-acgan-modified-auxiliary-classifie.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is discussed beyond a citation or used as a baseline.

paper-positive-unlabeled-learning-tensor.summary: This paper proposes a tensor-network model for positive unlabeled learning that classifies samples via feature-space distances to reference states and, unlike prior anomaly-detection tensor networks, can also generate new positive and negative instances. It is tested on MNIST and 15 categorical/mixed UCI datasets and outperforms GAN-based state-of-the-art baselines. CTGAN is cited only in passing in the introduction as an example of conditional-GAN methods applied to categorical tasks, not run in the experiments.

paper-missing-data-distribution-2023.summary: Argues that missingness itself carries information analysts need, which imputation and complete-case analysis both destroy before generation begins, and proposes HottGAN and MergeGAN to preserve the missing-pattern distribution alongside the observable one. Both are built directly on the CTGAN implementation, which is named as the GAN underneath them.

paper-privacy-protected-person-identific.summary: This paper addresses privacy leakage in person re-identification by proposing a Translation-Rendering-Sampling framework that generates virtual pedestrian images using privacy-irrelevant scene attributes (background, pose, illumination) instead of real captured appearances, trained on virtual samples like PersonX. The learned model is transferred to real target re-ID datasets without ever exposing person appearance during training. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of GAN-based methods prone to mode collapse, with no experimental use.
paper-privacy-protected-person-identific.needs: Full text not available; only a fragmentary citing sentence and abstract were provided, so the exact context and any deeper engagement with CTGAN cannot be confirmed. Industry classification is uncertain since person re-identification/surveillance is not explicitly listed.

paper-review-machine-learning-artificial.summary: A review article surveying machine learning and AI concepts and applications relevant to pediatric neurology, aimed at clinicians in that field. It covers general ML/AI topics likely including data augmentation and synthetic data generation as tools of interest to the specialty. CTGAN is cited as an example of synthetic data generation methods, with no evidence of it being run or evaluated.
paper-review-machine-learning-artificial.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is discussed or merely listed in a broader citation list of ML methods.

paper-synthesis-tax-return-datasets-2023.summary: This paper builds a pipeline that augments a small, privacy-restricted dataset of Thai-listed companies' financial statements to train tax-evasion detection models, using GAN-based synthesis and SMOTE for comparison, evaluated via correlation matrices, PCA, and a Quality Score. CTGAN is trained directly (40,000 epochs, batch size 250) to generate synthetic tax-return instances that are then labeled and used to train classifiers, with results compared against SMOTE-based augmentation. The paper also cites the SDV project's GitHub and its installable 'synthetic data vault' package as the source of this tooling.
paper-synthesis-tax-return-datasets-2023.needs: Unclear whether the 'synthetic data vault' package citation reflects actual use of the sdv library to obtain CTGAN, or is a loosely appended reference alongside the CTGAN paper citation.

paper-privacy-digital-marketing-2023.summary: Builds a user-modeling pipeline for a consent-based data monetization platform, embedding browsing behaviour into user representations, synthesizing those representations with a customized GAN so that marketing segments can be shared without exposing individuals, and evaluating downstream segmentation and targeting quality. CTGAN is not run: it is described in the related-work survey of tabular GAN variants as the conditional-generator approach to mixed continuous and discrete columns, and named again in future work as a variant the authors suggest trying instead of their own architecture.

paper-artificial-intelligence-universal-.summary: This paper explores the use of AI in higher education, building a use-case model on student assessment data that is expanded with a GAN-generated synthetic dataset and then classified using multiple ML algorithms (LR, LDA, KNN, CART, NB, SVM, RF), reaching 58% accuracy. The authors describe adopting 'a mechanism of GAN modeling... to tabulate the student data,' citing both the CTGAN and TGAN papers together for this step, without giving implementation or library details. The SDV-family tabular GAN work (CTGAN/TGAN) is cited as the basis for the GAN approach used to synthesize student records, but no code, hyperparameters, or package name confirm the sdv-dev library itself was run.
paper-artificial-intelligence-universal-.needs: Cannot confirm from evidence whether the authors ran the actual sdv-dev CTGAN/TGAN code or built their own GAN; no hyperparameters, imports, or architecture details are given.

paper-deep-neural-networks-tabular-2022.summary: A survey categorizing deep learning approaches for heterogeneous tabular data into data transformations, specialized architectures, and regularization models, and separately surveying deep generative approaches for tabular data synthesis; the authors also run an empirical benchmark of eleven deep learning methods against gradient-boosted trees on five real-world datasets. In its related-work discussion of tabular data generation, the survey describes SDV's CTGAN (its mode-specific normalization and conditional GAN architecture) and TVAE, and cites the original Synthetic Data Vault copula-based approach as classical prior art, without running any SDV code itself.
paper-deep-neural-networks-tabular-2022.needs: The tgan-2018 citation sentence in the evidence ('They often include missing values...') does not appear to genuinely engage with TGAN; likely a reference-numbering artifact, so tgan component was not included.

paper-generating-synthetic-sensor-event-.summary: This paper presents the IoT process log generator, a tool that produces synthetic event logs and synthetic IoT sensor event logs for process mining research, allowing users to configure processes, add controlled noise, and simulate diverse sensor types (motion, light, temperature, counter, on/off). It targets settings where real event logs are unavailable or of poor quality, and demonstrates the tool on two IoT-related use cases. The original Synthetic Data Vault paper is only listed in the reference list, cited generically alongside other synthetic-data works with no engagement or use in the tool.
paper-generating-synthetic-sensor-event-.needs: Full text or abstract needed to determine whether SDV was actually run (e.g., as a generator for sensor event logs) or merely cited as related work; current evidence only confirms a citation link.

paper-human-centric-artificial-intellige.summary: This paper proposes a human-centric AI reference architecture for Industry 5.0, integrating active learning, forecasting, explainable AI, simulated reality, and decision-making, validated on three real-world manufacturing case studies. SDV and CTGAN appear only in a background sentence in the introduction noting that GAN-based models, first applied to images, have since been extended to other data types. The Synthetic Data Vault and CTGAN papers are cited only as examples of this trend, with no synthetic data generation run or engaged with in the work.
paper-human-centric-artificial-intellige.needs: The DFKI affiliation type is judged as nonprofit research institute; could also be argued government-funded academic entity.

paper-overcoming-challenges-synthetic-ge.summary: This paper introduces UniformGAN, a differentially private GAN for tabular synthetic data generation that uses a uniform-distribution preprocessing step, SeLU activations, and Dense-Sparse-Dense training to better model unbalanced and long-tailed continuous columns. The authors also build an open-source command-line framework that generates and evaluates synthetic datasets from multiple models. CTGAN is run through this framework as one of the baseline generators (alongside TableGAN) and compared against UniformGAN across five real-world datasets on statistical similarity and privacy metrics.
paper-overcoming-challenges-synthetic-ge.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev/ctgan package or a custom reimplementation, so exact integration mechanism is inferred from abstract wording only.

paper-sorag-synthetic-sampling-strategy-.summary: This paper addresses imbalanced multi-label node classification in graphs (e.g., public transport networks) for remote-sensing applications, proposing a novel over-sampling framework that synthesizes both minority and unlabeled virtual samples exploiting graph topology, and shows it outperforms strong baselines on real-world network datasets. The work situates itself among minority over-sampling techniques for non-graph data, of which CTGAN is one cited example. CTGAN is only cited as related prior work on synthetic minority over-sampling, not run or extended in this study.
paper-sorag-synthetic-sampling-strategy-.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is discussed only in passing or engaged with more substantively as prior art for synthetic minority over-sampling.

paper-stress-testing-electrical-grids-20.summary: This paper proposes a GAN-based approach for generating synthetic multi-variate electrical grid load scenarios, using a novel dataset aggregating hourly electric generation data from several European countries to support grid stress-testing and planning. The authors evaluate their generative model with metrics designed to capture non-Gaussian, multimodal data distributions and compare its performance against a state-of-the-art tabular data generation model. TGAN, the SDV-family tabular synthesizer, is cited and used as the comparison baseline for their proposed GAN model.
paper-stress-testing-electrical-grids-20.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm the exact experimental setup or whether TGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or reimplemented, nor author affiliations.

paper-copula-synthetic-augmentation-mach.summary: This paper investigates whether copula-based statistical models can augment training data for machine-learning emulators in weather and climate applications, testing Gaussian, vine-parametric, and vine-nonparametric copulas on a toy downwelling-longwave-radiation model. Copula-augmented training sets reduced the neural-network emulator's mean absolute error by up to 62%. The authors' own copula implementations are used throughout; SDV's original paper is cited in the introduction as prior work showing copula-based models can generate synthetic data comparable to real data for privacy protection.
paper-copula-synthetic-augmentation-mach.needs: SDV (Patki et al. 2016) is cited only as related work on copula-based synthetic data generation; the paper's Gaussian/vine copula models appear to be its own implementation (likely via R copula packages, consistent with co-author Nagler's background), not SDV's GaussianCopula, so no SDV code is confirmed to run.

paper-benchmark-learned-systems-2021.summary: This paper argues that traditional database benchmarks are ill-suited to evaluate learned systems that adapt to changing workloads and data distributions, and proposes new metrics and design principles for benchmarking such systems. It is a position/discussion paper rather than an empirical study, outlining challenges like avoiding fixed workloads and capturing adaptability. SDV's founding paper is cited only in passing as prior work on synthetic data generation that a future high-fidelity synthesizer would need to extend.

paper-complexity-use-artificial-intellig.summary: This is a book chapter discussing the challenges and complexities of applying artificial intelligence methods in anatomic pathology, likely touching on data availability and synthetic data as a possible solution to limited training data. No experimental details, methods, or evaluation involving SDV are given in the available evidence. The SDV framework's original 2016 paper is only cited, with no indication it was run or engaged with in depth.
paper-complexity-use-artificial-intellig.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed substantively or merely listed among references. Placement based solely on metadata.

paper-generating-privacy-preserving-synt.summary: This paper proposes an oblivious variational autoencoder architecture for generating privacy-preserving synthetic tabular data, aiming to protect sensitive attributes while retaining statistical utility. It benchmarks its model against state-of-the-art deep generative baselines including medGAN, VEEGAN, tableGAN, CTGAN, and TVAE, and adopts mode-specific normalization (MSN) from CTGAN's methodology to preprocess multi-modal continuous variables. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE are run as comparison baselines, with TVAE singled out as the strongest competitor, while CTGAN's mode-specific normalization technique is also incorporated into the authors' own preprocessing pipeline.
paper-generating-privacy-preserving-synt.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev library itself or via the authors' own implementation of the published methodology.

paper-gan-actuarial-longtail-2020.summary: Argues that long-tail insurance risks are hard to price because the historical record contains too few severe events, and surveys how adversarial generation could synthesize rare-event representations to fill that gap, with a Wasserstein-style stabilization for the training dynamics. CTGAN is cited twice as the reference point for tabular adversarial generation and nothing more: the paper credits Xu et al. with preserving statistical attributes of tabular data while noting they did not address rare events, and misnames the model TabGAN in doing so.

paper-economic-feasibility-assessment-fr.summary: This paper proposes a framework combining Support Vector Machine and Genetic Algorithm to assess the commercial viability of underutilised crops in under-developed rural areas, using artificially generated training data from approximate crop models to compensate for scarce commercial crop data. The abstract describes GA-based synthetic training data generation but does not detail any SDV library usage. The work cites the original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) DSAA 2016 paper, apparently in relation to synthetic/artificial training data generation, without evidence of running it.
paper-economic-feasibility-assessment-fr.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV software was actually run or only cited as related work on synthetic data generation.

preprint-generative-framework-creation-m.summary: This preprint proposes a hierarchical diffusion-based generative framework to synthesize multi-attribute, geographically-explicit populations from aggregate-level census data, assigning explicit home and work locations and demonstrating improved joint-distribution reconstruction over Iterative Proportional Fitting and a one-shot diffusion baseline across U.S. states. The CTGAN paper is only listed in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs and is never run or engaged with in the body text.

paper-causal-residual-bootstrapping-2026.summary: Augments a small tabular dataset by resampling residuals along a known or estimated causal graph, so that added points respect the causal structure rather than only the observed joint distribution, and reports lower downstream error than both a no-augmentation baseline and generative augmenters, several of which prove worse than not augmenting at all. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five generative augmentation baselines run at 100 training samples across the reported error tables.

paper-privacy-postprocessing-synthetic-2.summary: Proposes a post-processing pipeline that can be slotted after any tabular generator, patching the categorical modes a generator collapses and then filtering samples that sit too close to a training record, and evaluates the trade-off it produces on a joint fidelity, utility and privacy protocol across three benchmarks. The pipeline is built and measured entirely on CTGAN and TVAE, tuned per dataset by Bayesian search, with the SDV implementation of the correct attribution probability supplying the privacy score.

paper-multilevel-monte-carlo-simulation-.summary: Sets out a framework for running Monte Carlo simulation studies on AI-generated data that has a multilevel structure, such as students nested in schools, and evaluates how well predictive performance and parameter recovery estimated on synthetic data track the real thing, adding fidelity criteria for within-table, between-table and machine learning utility. CTGAN is one of the two generators the framework is built on, trained on a joined single table after individual-level variables are split into cluster-mean and cluster-demeaned components, then corrected by a new cluster-level consistency alignment step that forces school-level variables to agree within a synthetic school without collapsing their marginals.

paper-network-attacks-adversarial-fideli.summary: Two tasks in one paper: classify network attacks with stable supervised models, then generate synthetic traffic with a spread of adversarial architectures — Vanilla-GAN, WGAN, WGAN-GP, KLD-GAN, CTGAN-2, a diffusion forest and an LLM — and ask which of them is worth keeping. The generators are the authors' own; the judgement is SDV's. Quality Report and Diagnostic Report percentages are averaged into an "SDV Overall Scores" table and a 95% threshold on those scores decides which models advance, so SDV is run as the evaluation harness the whole second half rests on.

preprint-not-all-jensen-shannon-2026.summary: This paper studies the measurement problem in estimating the Jensen-Shannon divergence for synthetic tabular data, showing that marginal-based estimators ignore joint dependencies while classifier-based estimators are highly sensitive to protocol choices such as calibration, dimensionality, and class imbalance. The authors derive a closed-form posterior correction for prior shift in classifier-based estimation and release an open-source estimator-aware evaluation tool, validating their analysis on controlled synthetic settings and on the Adult and Intrusion tabular benchmarks. CTGAN is used, alongside a VAE, as one of two generators producing the synthetic data on which the divergence estimators are empirically evaluated.
preprint-not-all-jensen-shannon-2026.needs: Unclear whether the authors generated the CTGAN synthetic data themselves via the sdv-dev package or reused data from the cited prior work [47]; treated as api_user based on direct use of CTGAN output.

preprint-saga-synthetic-agentic-graph-20.summary: SAGA is a four-phase pipeline for generating large-scale, semantically rich temporal graph benchmarks with automatic ground-truth anomaly labels, combining a scalable skeleton generator, LLM agents for domain semantics injection, and a state-alignment engine for conflict resolution. It targets applications like anti-money laundering, intrusion detection, and traffic forecasting where privacy and annotation costs limit real benchmark availability. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing as an example of tabular generators that produce rich semantics but fail to model graph structure or temporal dependencies, contrasting it with SAGA's approach.

preprint-synthetic-education-empirical-i.summary: This preprint benchmarks traditional resampling (SMOTE, Bootstrap, Random Oversampling) against deep generative models (Autoencoder, VAE, CopulaGAN) for generating synthetic student-performance data, evaluating distributional fidelity, ML utility (TSTR), and privacy (DCR). It finds resampling achieves high utility but no privacy protection, while VAE offers the best privacy-utility trade-off and CopulaGAN fails on continuous feature fidelity despite strong privacy. Both the VAE and CopulaGAN models were implemented and run directly via the SDV framework's fit()/sample() API with default hyperparameters and automatic metadata detection, making SDV's synthesizers two of the three deep generative methods carrying the paper's empirical results.

preprint-tabchange-precise-attribute-cha.summary: TabChange is a method for editing a single attribute of a tabular data instance so that the result remains natural and minimally changed, using an adversarial latent-space framework that removes information about the target attribute when its relationship with other attributes is strong. It is evaluated across seven datasets against counterfactual-generation baselines on validity, proximity, and naturalness metrics. The paper cites the original Synthetic Data Vault paper and the CTGAN paper in passing, in sentences about loss functions and network activations, with no SDV-family software run or engaged with in the text.

preprint-trustworthy-synthetic-campaign-.summary: This paper proposes strategy simulation fidelity (SSF), a decision-alignment metric for evaluating synthetic-data layers in marketing decision support systems, and PolicySynth, a generator conditioned on a production churn scorer to preserve decision-relevant structure. On telecommunications and banking corpora it benchmarks PolicySynth against several tabular generators, reporting mean SSF, seed-to-seed stability, membership-inference risk, and novel-record rate as a joint deployment gate. CTGAN and TVAE are run throughout as comparison baselines, with CTGAN's much wider seed-to-seed variance (SD 0.115 vs PolicySynth's 0.012) forming the paper's central stability argument.
preprint-trustworthy-synthetic-campaign-.needs: No explicit statement that the sdv-dev/ctgan package (vs. an independent implementation) was used to run CTGAN/TVAE; assumed api-like baseline use given no reimplementation details are given.

preprint-beyond-internal-constructing-co.summary: This paper proposes a method for constructing complete synthetic test datasets for fairness auditing by learning the joint distribution over two separate, overlapping real datasets, allowing demographic attributes to be paired with model features when no single complete dataset is accessible. It validates the synthetic data's fidelity and shows that fairness metrics computed on it match those from real data, using Adult, COMPAS and German Credit as test domains. CTGAN is run with default hyperparameters as a baseline generator trained on the full dataset for comparison, and the TVD Complement fidelity metric from the original SDV paper is used throughout to score synthetic data quality.

paper-pretactical-flight-delay-synthetic.summary: Asks whether synthetic flight records can stand in for proprietary operational data in pre-tactical delay and turnaround forecasting, training four generators on 1.74 million European flights and then comparing train-on-real against train-on-synthetic across five regression algorithms and three prediction tasks, and finds 94 to 97 percent of real-data predictive performance is retained. Two of the four generators are SDV code: CTGAN, whose mode-specific normalization the paper singles out for the multimodal delay distributions, and a Gaussian copula synthesizer, both carried in the companion library as adapted copies of sdv-dev sources over a declared RDT dependency.
paper-pretactical-flight-delay-synthetic.needs: the companion library SynthAIr/syntabair is itself an index candidate as a vendored_source repository and is not yet in the pool; the paper's Gaussian copula and fidelity metric names read as SDV and SDMetrics but the paper text credits neither, so the sdv-dev attribution here rests on the repository rather than on the paper

preprint-actionability-synthetic-heterog.summary: A population-based cohort study of 3735 adolescents and young adults with cancer that tests how sample size affects the 'actionability' (veracity, utility, and privacy concealment) of synthetic data generated at varying training and output sizes. The authors train four generator architectures — FastML, Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, and a DP-CGAN built atop SDV modules — on shrinking subsamples and evaluate the resulting synthetic datasets with prdc coverage/density metrics and SDMetrics' CAP algorithm for privacy risk. SDV's FastML and Gaussian Copula synthesizers, and its CTGAN implementation, are run directly as the study's evaluation generators, with SDMetrics supplying the attribute-inference privacy score.
preprint-actionability-synthetic-heterog.needs: DP-CGAN is described as 'built on top of existing SDV-library modules' but is not itself an official SDV synthesizer; not counted as a distinct SDV component.

preprint-advancing-retail-science-compre.summary: This paper proposes an evaluation framework for synthetic retail data along three axes -- fidelity, utility, and privacy -- applied to five generative models trained on a retail basket dataset (Complete Journey). It distinguishes stability from generalizability for fidelity, tests downstream classification utility, and uses differential-privacy-style distance metrics for privacy. CTGAN is run as one of five tabular generative models benchmarked across all three evaluation axes, with its mode-specific normalization discussed as a mechanism for handling imbalanced categorical distributions.

preprint-inference-combining-rules-multi.summary: This paper studies whether combining-rule methods developed for multiple-imputation-style inference can be validly applied to statistical analysis of differentially private synthetic (DIPS) datasets, testing several DP synthesizers (DataSynthesizer, COPULA-SHIRLEY, DP-CTGAN, PATE-CTGAN, DPGAN) across simulated datasets to see when variance estimators give accurate coverage. The empirical work runs DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN, descendants of CTGAN built by other authors, rather than CTGAN itself. CTGAN (and its precursor TGAN) is cited and its mode-specific normalization and conditional generator design are described in prose as the basis these descendant methods modify, but CTGAN itself is never run.

preprint-autodiff-combining-auto-encoder.summary: This paper proposes AutoDiff, a tabular data synthesizer that combines an autoencoder for handling heterogeneous features with a diffusion model in the resulting latent space, aiming to improve statistical fidelity and downstream ML utility over prior GAN- and diffusion-based synthesizers. The authors benchmark AutoDiff against CTGAN, TVAE, CTABGAN+, Stasy, and TabDDPM across 15 public tabular datasets on fidelity, ML efficacy, and privacy metrics. CTGAN and TVAE, both citing the SDV-family CTGAN paper, are run as baseline synthesizers among several comparison models, not modified or extended.

paper-margctgan-low-sample-2023.summary: Observes that synthetic tabular data is usually judged only by downstream task usefulness and that this hides how models behave when the real sample is small, then evaluates several generators across fidelity, utility and marginal statistics in the low-sample regime, finding CTGAN strong on attribute fidelity but weak on utility while TableGAN is the reverse. MargCTGAN is the paper's answer to that split: it is built on CTGAN and adds feature matching of decorrelated marginals in the principal component space, keeping the rest of the model, and improves utility without giving up the fidelity CTGAN already had.

paper-rct-twin-gan-2023.summary: Simulates randomized trial effects in real-world populations by generating a digital twin of a trial whose covariate patterns match an electronic health record, addressing the historical underrepresentation of key groups in trial cohorts. The model is CTGAN modified: an adapted loss and multi-covariate conditioning are layered onto its conditional architecture, making this a named clinical derivative rather than a use.

preprint-discriminator-gan-tabular-synth.summary: A preprint proposing a bi-discriminator GAN architecture for synthesizing tabular data, addressing limitations of prior single-discriminator GAN approaches to tabular synthesis. The paper positions its method relative to prior tabular-GAN work in the field. CTGAN is cited as prior art in tabular data synthesis, though the evidence does not show whether it was run experimentally.

No further methodological detail is available beyond the metadata and citation record. The work cites the original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) 2016 paper as a reference for synthetic data generation.

preprint-composable-generative-models-20.summary: This preprint introduces the Composable Generative Model (CGM), a transformer-based autoregressive architecture in which any conditional generative sub-model can be nested to jointly generate heterogeneous tabular data (numerical, categorical, image, text, sequence) with privacy-preserving applications in mind. The authors evaluate CGM against 14 recent generative models across 13 datasets using the public SDGym benchmark and leaderboard, reporting it beats prior tabular generators including CTGAN, TVAE and CopulaGAN. SDGym is run directly as the benchmarking harness, and CTGAN/TVAE/CopulaGAN (SDV-family synthesizers) serve as the baseline models CGM is compared against on likelihood and ML-efficacy metrics.

preprint-standardised-metrics-methods-sy.summary: This preprint proposes a unified pipeline of metrics and methods for evaluating synthetic tabular data along resemblance, utility, and privacy dimensions, tested across six healthcare-related datasets using four synthetic tabular data generation approaches. In its background section it surveys prior deep-learning-based synthesis methods, characterising the Synthetic Data Vault as an ensemble of probabilistic graphical and deep-learning techniques and CTGAN as a GAN-based approach for numerical, binary, and categorical data. Both SDV and CTGAN are cited only as prior art in the related-work discussion, without evidence in the available text that either was run in the experiments.

paper-dp-heterogeneous-ehr-2020.summary: Explores generative adversarial training for synthetic electronic health records that mix binary, categorical and continuous administrative and diagnostic fields, selects a WGAN-GP formulation over MedGAN and WGAN on data-fidelity grounds, and then retrains it under (1, 1e-5) differential privacy, reporting a roughly 17% drop in downstream readmission-classification utility and a sub-population analysis showing no bias introduced beyond what the source data already carried. CTGAN was trained as a candidate generator and dropped for slow training and poorer results on the paper's high-cardinality discrete features, but its mode-specific normalization is retained: the real-valued columns are decomposed with Gaussian mixture models as in CTGAN before the surviving WGAN-GP model is fitted.

repo-ai-agents-projects-tutorials.summary: A collection of agent tutorials covering multi-agent systems, memory, planning and reasoning loops, with one notebook devoted to synthetic data creation. That notebook is an end-to-end SDV walkthrough: `Metadata`, `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer` and `evaluate_quality` are used in sequence, so the tutorial teaches the full fit-sample-score loop rather than one call.
